newsitem.title: THAILAND: FAO asks Thailand to cooperate in food programme.
newsitem.headline: FAO asks Thailand to cooperate in food programme.

text.p: The U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation asked Thailand on Tuesday to consider taking part in south-south agricultural production and trade to ensure global food security.
The call was made by visiting FAO director-general Jacques Diouf who said programmes had been set up for developing countries to share experience and expertise to boost food sufficency.
Diouf told reporters Asian countries that participated in such programmes included China, Indonesia, India and Vietnam.

The move to boost south-south cooperation followed the World Food Summit in November last year when participants pledged to work to reduce the number of undernourished people in the world to half the present level by 2015.
It is estimated that there are 800 million people worldwide currently without adequate access to food.
"We try to create an environment that would allow us to feed a growing world population as there would be three billion more people on earth by the year 2001," he said.
Diouf said he had asked the Thai government and private sector to consider participating in south-south cooperation.

"We are encouraging people from developing countries to provide assistance to other developing countries in view of the fact that they have acquired experience...of dealing with the same issues," he said.
